# pangolin_site_provisioning_key (Resource)

Manages a site provisioning key (Pangolin 1.17+, Enterprise): a Newt started with `--provisioning-key <key>` registers a new site by itself, without creating the site first.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Newt started with `--provisioning-key` creates its own site.
resource "pangolin_site_provisioning_key" "homelab" {
  name              = "homelab-hosts"
  max_batch_size    = 5
  valid_until       = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  approve_new_sites = false
}

output "newt_provisioning_key" {
  value     = pangolin_site_provisioning_key.homelab.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The key name. The server cannot rename a key: changing it replaces the key.

### Optional

- `approve_new_sites` (Boolean) Whether sites created with the key are approved right away; `false` leaves them pending approval in the dashboard. Defaults to `true`.
- `max_batch_size` (Number) How many sites the key can create in total. Unset means no limit.
- `valid_until` (String) Expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp, e.g. `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Unset means no expiry.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was created.
- `id` (String) The provisioning key ID.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The key to give Newt. Only returned on creation: empty after import.
- `last_chars` (String) The last characters of the key, as shown in the dashboard.
- `last_used` (String) When the key was last used, null if never.
- `num_used` (Number) How many sites the key has created.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a site provisioning key by its ID. The key itself is not returned after import.
terraform import pangolin_site_provisioning_key.homelab <site_provisioning_key_id>
```
